newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Appeal hearing starts for S.Korean ex-presidents.
newsitem.headline: Appeal hearing starts for S.Korean ex-presidents.

text.p: The appeals session started on Monday in the trial of South Korea's two former presidents who face mutiny and treason charges stemming from a 1979 coup and the massacre of pro-democracy protesters the following year.
Chun Doo Hwan and his immediate successor, Roh Tae-woo, stood side by side before the panel of judges, who read out a summary of the appeal statements, witnesses said.
Judges approved requests from the prosecution and defence lawyers to summon 33 people to testify at the trial, which resumes on October 14, a court official said.
Included in the list are Choi Kyu-hah, who led the caretaker government between late 1979 and early 1980. Choi has maintained a low profile since that time.
Choi, requested as a witness by both prosecution and defence lawyers, would be asked to appear in court on October 28, the court official said.
In August, Chun and Roh, who were also convicted of taking hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes, were sentenced to death and 22-1/2 years in prison, respectively.
They are appealing to have their convictions dismissed while state prosecutors are demanding Roh's sentence be increased to life in jail as they had sought at the initial trial.
Fourteen former aides to Chun and Roh will also battle prosecutors trying to increase their sentences, which range from suspended jail terms to 10 years in prison.
Monday's session focused on declaring the opening of the appeals trial.
